title: What Are Young Men Missing?
author: Institute for Family Studies
summary: This IFS newsletter examines marital horizons as a key factor in young men's developmental trajectories, analyzes contemporary representations of romance, and reports on counterintuitive findings about community support and family formation. The collection suggests that young men's clarity about marriage prospects significantly influences educational and career investment.
points: Marital horizons significantly influence young men's motivation structures and educational investment patterns. The experience of community support may depend more on network presence and shared values than on frequency of material assistance. Fertility decline in the U.S. is broad-based, cutting across traditional demographic and educational lines. Cultural representations of romance both reflect and shape young adult expectations about relationship formation. Data on marriage and family stability should inform political and policy discussions across the ideological spectrum.
quotes: One of the most consequential factors of young men's developmental trajectories is the clarity or uncertainty of their marital horizons.
The parents who feel most supported by their communities are the ones leaning on those communities the least.
The decline in fertility in the United States is a broad, population-wide shift that cuts across education lines.
Religious community continues to produce a different sequence of family formation than surrounding secular culture.
